So, you're interested in pitching a product to Drop Dead Studios? You can contact Adam Meyers through the official fan Discord server (see the link in the sidebar). When doing so, answer the following questions to help the team at DDS better understand who you are and what exactly you're proposing.

**Have you created any type of content for a game before?** (There's a long history of making homebrew content for games like the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game and Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition. In fact, many writers get started by making things for their home games, then looking to officially publish things. If you have created any homebrewed content, please include a link to some of it (if possible) so the team can take a look at the creative side of things. Don't forget to include any context that may help explain it - something that would be wildly inappropriate for general publishing may be perfectly appropriate for the context of a home game it was made to be used in.)

**Have you ever published a tabletop RPG product before?** (You don't need to be experienced to publish through DDS, but published writers usually have more familiarity with the process of releasing products. If you have published something, please include a little information about it and, if possible, a link to a web store page showing it. DriveThruRPG is preferred for this when possible, but we understand that not all products are sold in all storefronts. Authors who have previous publishing experience may require less in the way of manuscripts and samples before getting approval to write something.)

**How familiar are you with DDS' products?** (You don't have to be an expert who can recite every detail of every rule off the top of your head, though we'll be impressed if you can. However, DDS does have certain expectations when it comes to theme and balance, and it's important to have a thorough understanding of how any new content is intended to interact with existing content.)

**What sort of content do you want to write for DDS?** (Different people write different sorts of things. For example, some people focus on content for Spheres of Might, while others focus on expanding existing systems and making magic items. Some authors are fully capable of writing many different types of content, but having an interest and an objective with your writing helps. It's okay to write different things later, but try to limit your initial pitch to a single idea for a product. The [[Creating New Spheres]] page has some information about making that type of content. Include the product type you want to write, as described below, in your answer for this.)

**Do you have some or all of a manuscript ready to show?** (Creating products to release for Spheres of Power/Might, or other systems, is more complex than many newcomers believe, and some people never complete their first manuscript. If you have at least some of a product ready to show, this will get you more attention, and faster, than merely giving a proposal. DDS only expects text in manuscripts; you are not expected to do art, layout, or other publishing duties. We broadly prefer manuscripts to be linked through Google Documents.)

**Do you have something other than writing that you'd like to do?** (Sometimes people don't come in to write a specific product, but rather to offer other services or skills. For example, you might want to offer your skills as an artist, or to code material for an online character builder.)

**Are you familiar with the Open Game License?** (If not, you can read a copy of it on the Wiki's Legal page, available on the right-hand sidebar. DDS publishes almost everything under the terms of this license, and you should be familiar with Product Identity, Open Game Content, and generally what you can or cannot do when writing a manuscript. Neither the Wiki's administrator nor DDS are lawyers and cannot give you legal advice about the OGL, but it is important that you take the time to understand it. You may also need to review other licenses, such as the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Compatibility License.)

---

## What To Expect

**Review Processes:** No product is perfect on its first draft. Spheres products may go through a public playtesting phase for weeks or even months before release. Be willing to accept criticism about your writing, and sometimes the need to rewrite large portions of content. This is a normal part of the publishing process, and even the most experienced writers go through this.

**Payment:** Pay from DDS generally comes when a product is released, especially if it's being funded by the Patreon model. Given the release schedule, this may mean you'll be waiting for payment for quite some time after you finish writing. Payment terms beyond this are not disclosed publicly.

**Confidentiality:** DDS and its team will respect your privacy. You are expected to reciprocate this. Any discussions with the company owner or the other writers should be treated as confidential and not discussed with others. Among other things, this helps to protect the reputations of everyone involved and prevents outsiders from misunderstanding things mentioned out-of-context.

---

## Drop Dead Studios Product Types

**Spheres Apocrypha:** Spheres Apocrypha are about 1000 words long (with 10 pieces of smaller content, not 1-2 large pieces) and focus on a single concept. If you haven't published anything before, writing one of these is a good way to get started. These are generally faster and easier to release.

**Handbooks:** Handbooks are about 15,000 words long and include a significant amount of new content. These are usually themed and may have class archetypes, new talents, new spheres, magical items, feats, etc. Most handbooks include multiple types of material. Try to avoid going over the word count limits, by the way, unless it is necessary for the product to be complete.

**Other Products:** Drop Dead Studios may publish other products, such as GM screens or other physical goods. These are typically evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and may require more experience creating products. It may also publish books longer than handbooks, although these are usually negotiated on a case-by-case basis.
